rationale: A wins because it knows where the facts stop. Its "Mercury Personal runs on partner banks, not a charter — what that means for your money" is narrow, sourceable, and gated by the exact missing proof; B's "A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones" imports a whole neobank obituary the update never supplied. B has sharper swagger, but swagger is not sourcing.
gaps_in_A: "same arrangement that has drawn scrutiny across consumer fintech" imports outside regulatory context; plausible, but not in the update and needs sourcing before it becomes load-bearing.

"Why a profitable startup bank is going downmarket to individuals" should keep saying "the company says it is profitable" unless Mercury provides a definition or financials. The set asks for that proof, but the headline still sounds too settled.

A underplays the best SVB-adjacent lens: whether crisis-era trust with startups transfers to retail depositors. It mentions SVB as origin context but does not fully develop that as its own consumer-trust story.
"Every kept angle currently leans on undisclosed numbers" overstates the weakness. The partner-bank structure angle needs partner/disclosure facts more than pricing or deposit targets.
gaps_in_B: "A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones" is the big sin. The update says Mercury claims profitability; it says nothing proving consumer neobanks were broken by this market.

"The startup bank that grew on SVB's collapse now wants your paycheck" overreaches. Checking and savings do not automatically mean direct deposit, payroll capture, or an existing-customer paycheck strategy.

"Mercury opens consumer accounts to customers it doesn't hold deposits for" is too cute and technically muddy. The fact is partner-bank provision, not that Mercury somehow has customers it does not hold deposits for.
"the same arrangement that has been the live question in fintech-banking supervision" creates a current regulatory peg without evidence from the update. Good reporter bait, bad discipline.
